title: The CLI test helper doesn't pair --json and --plain by default, so a renderer divergence between them needs someone to remember to check both
description:
Follow-up from QCLI-272, filed per opum-agent's suggestion rather than folded into that (closed) task -- work discovered outside a task's acceptance criteria is a new task, not a silent addition.

QCLI-272 was a --json/--plain divergence: --json was always correct (JSON.stringify drops an undefined-valued property) and --plain leaked the JS value underneath it (Object.entries keeps it). The bug survived because most existing tests exercise one output mode or the other, not the same invocation through both -- the divergence class, not just this one mechanism, had no structural test coverage forcing both surfaces to be checked together.

QCLI-272's own new end-to-end test (test/qcli272-init-plain-omits-undefined.test.ts) asserts BOTH --plain (no literal undefined) and --json (both keys correctly absent) for the same invocation, but it does this ad hoc in one test file. The question this task is scoped to answer: should pairing --json and --plain assertions be the DEFAULT shape for CLI-process output tests, via the shared test helper, so a future divergence fails without anyone remembering to write the second assertion.

Not a decision to make on faith -- look at how many of the existing CLI-process tests (test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts and siblings) already call the same command in both modes with separate assertions versus how many only ever exercise one mode, before deciding whether a shared helper is worth the refactor or whether the ad hoc pattern QCLI-272 used is enough given how rare the underlying mechanism is.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A count is taken of existing CLI-process tests that exercise only one output mode for a given command versus both, so the decision below is made from that count rather than impression.

A decision is recorded either way: build a shared test-helper shape that runs a command through both --json and --plain and asserts on both by default, or explicitly decline to given the count, with the reason written down.
If built, at least the commands sharing renderHumanPayload's object-literal pattern (quest init and any future command found to use it) are migrated to the shared shape.
If declined, this task still leaves a written trail explaining why, so the next --json/--plain divergence does not have to rediscover the same question opum-agent raised on QCLI-272.
